$comment: The error taxonomy every SDK maps: every code dsp-backend can send an API-key caller (the `code = "..."` of each DspError subclass under dsp-backend src/dsp, at the commit spec/openapi.json names). Staff-only and internal codes (privacy.*), and the Tools API's (tools.*: /tools/v1, outside the published /v1/* paths), are left out. `concept` is the language-neutral name conformance cases use; each SDK maps it to an idiomatic class. `retry` is normative: an SDK that retries a code marked false is a bug. A code may be sent with a status other than its usual one (request.invalid on a 400, 404 or 405): map by code, and by status only when the code is unknown.
type_uri_rule: docs_base + code with '.' and '_' replaced by '-'
notes: Branch on `code`. Never on `title` or `detail`: those are prose and may be reworded.
Problem bodies omit null fields, so any field except type/title/status/code may be absent. `errors` (field-level validation detail) and `extra` are top-level and present only when they have content.
An unrecognised code falls back to the class for the HTTP status, never raises.
402 and 429 are never conflated. 402 is commercial and carries no Retry-After; waiting does not help.
Every response, success or error, carries the request id in the X-Request-Id header. A caller's own X-Request-Id is kept if it matches [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}.

status_fallbacks.$comment: Used when a response carries a code this SDK version does not know (or none, as from a proxy). Never raise on an unknown code.

codes.meaning: A finished run's rows are kept for a limited time; these are gone. Start the run again for fresh results.
No agent run with that id in this workspace.

The key is valid but lacks the scope this route needs. A key created without scopes has dsp.search.read, dsp.entities.read and dsp.usage.read; agent runs need dsp.agents.read / dsp.agents.write granted explicitly.

Every authentication failure, collapsed into one answer: no credential, an unknown, revoked or expired key, a key sent from a browser (any request with an Origin header), a key sent together with a bearer token. Deliberately indistinguishable so a caller cannot probe keys. The real reason is logged against request_id. A revoked key keeps working until the backend's cached token for it expires (at most about 5 minutes).
Credentials cannot be checked right now (the auth service or its signing keys are unreachable). Transient; Retry-After: 1.
A signed-in user (a dashboard token, never an API key) has not chosen a workspace. Choosing one at the auth service fixes it; signing in again does not.
This Idempotency-Key already started another credit purchase. Purchases are dashboard-only; an API key never gets this far.

The workspace cannot pay for this call. Nothing was charged and the answer is withheld. `extra` carries `available_credits` and `required_credits`. No Retry-After: waiting does not help, buying credits does. Never retried, never conflated with a 429.
Auto top-up needs the card a dashboard purchase saves, and there is none. Dashboard-only.
Buying credits and saving auto top-up take a signed-in owner or billing member; an API key is always refused.
The credits ledger refused to hold credits for this work (an agent run or an enrichment start), so it did not run and nothing was charged. A repeat cannot help: contact support with the request_id.

The credit ledger is unreachable and the backend cannot vouch for this workspace's credits (no recent balance, it does not cover the call, or the workspace already owes the most allowed while the ledger is down). Nothing was charged and the answer is withheld. Retry-After: 30. Also the answer to an agent run start while the ledger is down.
Sprouts staff froze this workspace's wallet: nothing can be charged until it is unfrozen. Contact support. Never retried.
This Idempotency-Key already started an enrichment job or lookup with another body. Send a new key for a new job; reuse one only to retry the same request.
A cancel of an enrichment job that has already ended. The API answers with the job instead, so a caller rarely sees it.
No enrichment job with that id in this workspace.
An enrichment job's rows are kept for 7 days after it ends; these are gone. Start a new job to enrich them again.
No such export job for this workspace, or its file has expired (exports are kept 24 hours).
More rows than one export may hold. Export a narrower range (`offset`, `limit`).
No such feedback report for this caller.
The search or run a report names does not exist, or is not this caller's. One code for both on purpose: distinguishing them would say whether another workspace's search exists.
No history entry with that id for this caller. A 404 rather than a 403 even when the row belongs to someone else: confirming it exists would leak that it does.
An unexpected server error. Bounded retry is reasonable; a billed call is charged only as its last step.
A list holds one kind of record, set when it is created or by its first add. These items are of another kind.
Over a size limit: lists per workspace, items per list, or a free workspace's saved-items cap. Nothing was added.
A list with this name already exists in the workspace. Names are unique per workspace, ignoring case.
No such saved list in this workspace. Missing, deleted and another workspace's list are deliberately the same answer.
The server cannot do this yet (today: listing agent runs, until the engine serves its run list). The request is not the problem; retrying will not help.

The domain or LinkedIn page names more than one company with people. Nothing was charged. `extra.identifier`, `extra.candidate_count` and `extra.candidates` (each with `company_ref`, `name`, `domain`, `linkedin_url`) let the caller pick one and ask again with its `company_ref`.
The cursor is older than 24 hours. Run the request again from the first page.

The cursor is malformed, failed signature verification, or does not match this request. A cursor is signed against the request that produced it: resend every field unchanged (and `limit` too on routes whose cursor binds it).
Paging beyond 10,000 results. Narrow the request instead.

Too many calls to one operation from this workspace or key in the current minute. `extra` carries `limit`, `window`, `operation`, `scope` and `retry_after`; X-RateLimit-* and RateLimit-* headers carry the limit, what remains and the reset in seconds. Honour Retry-After.

This credential already has as many agent runs going as it may (two), or the engine is running as many as it takes. Sent with Retry-After, but never retried: a run takes minutes, so follow or cancel one, then start again.
A relationship anchor named more than one company or institution. `extra.anchor` and `extra.candidates` list the choices; name it more precisely (a domain or LinkedIn URL rather than a name).
A relationship anchor matched no company or institution.
A department or seniority the taxonomy does not hold. `extra.allowed` lists the values it takes.

The request is invalid. Validation failures carry the field-level detail in the top-level `errors` array (`loc`, `msg`, `type`); `detail` names the fields. The server forbids unknown body fields. Also the code of a 400 (a missing or unusable Idempotency-Key on an agent run start) and of a routing refusal (404 unknown path, 405 wrong method), with that status.
The request is larger than the route accepts: a Tools body over its cap, or an enrichment lookup with more rows than the workspace's lookups take (start a job instead). Send a smaller request.
A relationships question the network cannot answer as asked. `extra.kind` says which refusal and `extra.try_instead`, when present, suggests a rewording.
This server is at its in-flight limit. Transient; Retry-After: 1.
The backend's own stores cannot answer right now. Transient; Retry-After: 1.
The work did not finish within the request's time budget. It is abandoned and not charged.
A service behind the API could not be reached or failed. Nothing was charged: a billed call is charged only once its answer is ready.
